title: Service accounts: impersonation, and why a downloaded key is the last resort

videos.script: A service account is two things at once. It holds roles, like a person. And it is a resource, that other people hold roles on. {{two}} The second half is where it gets dangerous. Whoever may act as the account holds every role the account holds. {{actas}} There are three ways to prove you are a service account. {{three}} The best is to attach it to a machine. The machine asks for a token, and no key exists anywhere. {{attached}} The next is impersonation. A person asks Google for a token in the account's name. It lasts an hour, and the log says who borrowed it. {{borrow}} In your lab, gcloud asks Google for exactly that token, and Google refuses the placeholder. You will read the method it names. {{refusal}} The last is a downloaded key. It is a file, it never expires, and it works for anybody who has a copy. {{key}} So it is the last resort. And if one leaks, you delete it first and ask questions second. {{end}}
